title: Execute Emergency Thruster Burn
desc: Spend $20M in propellant reserves to raise the orbital periapsis immediately, guaranteeing spacecraft safety.

title: Power Down & Ride It Out
desc: Shut down all non-essential science instruments and tuck solar arrays to survive the thermal spike.

title: Push Through for Atmospheric Data
desc: Keep sensors active inside the storm to gather rare upper-atmosphere telemetry for future landers.

title: Rapid Thruster Pulse Sequence
desc: Fire high-impulse attitude thrusters to shake the hinge loose without draining extra funds.

title: Dedicated Deep Space Network (DSN) Diagnostic
desc: Lease emergency DSN tracking time for $25M to run slow thermal-cycling maneuvers that safely free the boom.

title: Jettison & Recalibrate
desc: Detach the jammed radar boom and rebalance the orbiter around its remaining cameras.

title: Emergency Software Compression Patch
desc: Upload an experimental AI compression patch for $10M to shrink image files before transmission.

title: Relay Through Legacy Orbiters
desc: Pay $45M in inter-agency bandwidth fees to offload image queues to older Mars orbiters.

title: Purge Low-Priority Telemetry
desc: Delete background weather and engineering logs to free up drive space for flagship surface photos.

title: Full Avionics Reboot
desc: Power-cycle the instrument bus, risking a permanent hardware lockup on a vulnerable sensor.

title: Ground-Team Software Recalibration
desc: Spend $15M on flight-software engineers to write a dead-pixel filter around the damaged sensor.

title: Gemini-Assisted AI Reconstruction
desc: Run the damaged sensor's raw counts through a Gemini-derived vision model on the ground, rebuilding usable climate data from surrounding pixels at minimal cost.

title: Emergency Instrument Shutdown
desc: Cut power to high-draw cameras like HiRISE and CRISM to keep thermal heaters and radios alive.

title: Overdrive Heaters on Reserve Batteries
desc: Keep science cameras warm for immediate post-storm imaging at the risk of deep battery degradation.

title: Reroute Ka-Band Transmitter Power
desc: Throttle communications down to bare-minimum telemetry while leasing $15M in high-sensitivity Earth receiving dishes.

title: Maximum Retropropulsion Burn
desc: Fire landing thrusters early at 100% thrust, burning through reserve fuel and kicking up heavy surface debris.

title: Jettison Secondary Science Cargo
desc: Dump non-essential rover hardware mid-air to lighten the lander for a safe touchdown.

title: Automated Diversion to Flat Plains
desc: Redirect the lander away from the rocky target zone toward safer terrain, requiring a $40M rover recovery plan later.

title: Deploy Maintenance Rovers for Hard Reset
desc: Command surface rovers to physically inspect and reconnect external power lines to backup coolers.

title: Launch Emergency Top-Off Tanker
desc: Fast-track a $150M mini-tanker on the next available launch window to replenish lost fuel.

title: Throttle Down ISRU Production
desc: Reduce fuel plant output to preserve remaining propellant, forcing a leaner ascent margin later.

title: Rely on Orbital Map Matching (TRN)
desc: Switch incoming landers to autonomous Terrain Relative Navigation using orbital photos.

title: Dispatch Rover to Clear & Reboot Beacon
desc: Send an autonomous rover across rough terrain to brush off solar arrays and jumpstart the beacon.

title: Upload High-Priority Orbital Scans
desc: Spend $30M on dedicated orbiter imaging passes to build a 5-cm hazard map of the landing zone.

title: High-Pressure Backflush
desc: Cycle the compressor in reverse to blow dust out of the valve, risking a seal rupture.

title: Switch to Backup Atmospheric Intake
desc: Reroute CO2 collection through secondary filters at half production speed.

title: Ship Replacement Valve with Crew
desc: Pack a $30M spare valve assembly onto the crew lander for a Day-1 EVA repair.

title: Over-Pressurize Air Tanks
desc: Pump reserve nitrogen into the module to force the layers apart, straining the pressure seals.

title: Thermal Cycling & Slow Inflation
desc: Rotate the ship to let solar heat soften the polymer foam over several hours while mission control monitors telemetry.

title: Manual Astronaut EVA Inspection
desc: Send crew members outside to manually inspect and free the jammed folds.
